notable_absence.finding: This page never states an ordering precondition on the database-offline/online operations themselves (they are the base primitive, not built on top of anything else), nor does it describe them as bypassing any normal/automatic schedule - there is no automatic online/offline transition described anywhere on this page except at Sync Gateway startup (see the 'Starting with a Database Offline' section), which is a one-time default rather than a recurring schedule a manual call could pre-empt.

cross_component_finding: The change of status (online or offline) of a database occurs only in the specific Sync Gateway instance addressed. It's not reflected by other Sync Gateway instances using that database. If you want to make changes in multiple Sync Gateway instances, you need to coordinate individual change operations in each instance. This instance-level/database-level distinction is genuinely new vocabulary with no precedent in round 3's access-control extraction, which never described database-level (as opposed to document/channel/user-level) state at all - directly supporting this round's hypothesis that manage/ holds vocabulary neither the access-control docs nor any reference/conceptual page ever needed.
cross_product_finding: None on this page specifically - it is entirely Sync-Gateway-internal state machine description, with no comparison drawn to Couchbase Server or Capella's own online/offline concepts (which round 26 found under manage/ as failover/node-recovery states). The shape is structurally similar (a state machine reachable only via manage/) but the page draws no explicit parallel.
